title: FoxRun Activation Kickoff - Redwood Onboarding
summary: Initial implementation kickoff for FoxRun Logistics. Reviewed high-level onboarding plan, network and security constraints for a VPC/private deployment, initial throughput and latency targets, success criteria for pilot, and next steps for access, benchmark run, and pricing. Agreement to run a 2-week pilot with dedicated capacity and a follow-up benchmarking session next Tuesday.
topics: Initial pilot scope and success metrics
action_items: Erik Mercer - Share current infra diagram and CIDR ranges - 2026-08-26
Liam Turner - Prepare baseline benchmark script and runbook - 2026-08-25
Priya Patel - Send onboarding playbook and pricing summary - 2026-08-24
Samir Gupta - Grant staging VPC access / create temporary firewall rules - 2026-08-26
Olivia Chen - Confirm pilot success criteria and data sample details - 2026-08-27
next_steps: Redwood to provision dedicated trial cluster and share credentials
Customer to provide network diagram and list of stakeholders
Schedule benchmarking run the week of 2026-08-31
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-23
Start time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Aisha Khan, Liam Turner, Priya Patel (Redwood); Erik Mercer, Nina Alvarez, Samir Gupta, Olivia Chen (FoxRun)

[00:00] Aisha (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I think we have, like, 45-ish minutes on the calendar. Quick intros and then we'll jump into the kickoff plan. I'm Aisha, AE, and with me is Liam, our solutions eng, and Priya, who'll be your CSM through the pilot.

[00:18] Erik (FoxRun - CTO): Thanks Aisha, Erik here. We'll keep this super focused. I'm joined by Nina, Samir, and Olivia. We're excited but a bit pressed on timeline, so we'll want to nail down the pilot cadence.

[00:32] Priya (Redwood CSM): Hi all. The playbook I shared earlier has the week-by-week milestones. We'll adapt it to FoxRun specifics today.

[00:45] Liam (Redwood SE): Great. I want to make sure we capture the infra constraints up front — is the plan still to run Redwood Private in your VPC, or are we considering dedicated hosted for the trial?

[01:02] Nina (Head of ML): We prefer private in our VPC due to data residency and compliance. We do have a firewall team so there will be some rules to open.

[01:15] Samir (SRE): Yeah, we'll need IP ranges and port info. We run strict egress rules, so we'll probably whitelist things.

[01:28] Liam: Understood. For VPC deployment we typically need CIDR ranges, allowed egress to our control plane, and SSH-ish tunnels only if we do on-prem. For cloud VPC it's more about peering and routes. I'll list the exact ports in the access checklist.

[01:50] Olivia (PM): Can you clarify what "dedicated" implies here? From a cost and latency standpoint — what are the tradeoffs?

[02:02] Aisha: Sure. Dedicated means reserved GPU pools for your pilot — predictable throughput, lower noisy neighbor risk, and we can tune batching and KV cache behavior. Hosted is faster to onboard but shares capacity. If latency consistency matters, dedicated is usually preferred.

[02:25] Erik: Our main KPIs for the pilot are 99th pct latency under 350ms for short prompts, and total per-token cost under our budget. We want both a cost and latency baseline.

[02:40] Liam: Makes sense. We'll capture baseline workloads — average tokens per request, sequence lengths, concurrency. Nina, can you share representative prompt examples and typical sequence lengths?

[02:55] Nina: Yeah, most of our queries are 120-320 tokens, some long-form summarization up to 1,200 tokens but those are batched overnight. Real-time is mostly short.

[03:10] Aisha: Good to know. For short-form realtime we can prioritize low-latency model variants and tighter batching windows. For longer async jobs, we can recommend quantized variants to reduce cost.

[03:24] Samir: On security — we have SOC2 in our roadmap, and our security team will audit logs. How do you handle audit logs and KMS integration?

[03:36] Priya: We integrate with customer KMS providers for Private deployments, and we can provide access logs/audit trails with retention options. I can share our security pack which includes SOC2 certs and a KMS integration guide.

[03:50] Erik: Do you support customer-managed keys (CMKs) and HSM-backed stores?

[03:57] Liam: Yes, for Private we support CMKs via standard cloud KMS and can plug into HSMs depending on the customer's environment. There may be a short integration window for exchange of policies. We'll note that as an action.

[04:12] Olivia: Also, SSO and RBAC — our product team needs SCIM and SAML so we can provision access to our operators.

[04:21] Priya: We do SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning for enterprise plans. We'll collect the IdP metadata after this call.

[04:34] [crosstalk briefly, inaudible]

[04:50] Aisha: Okay next — pilot scope. We propose a two-week pilot: week one smoke tests and baseline benchmarks, week two focused load/latency testing and integration with your staging. Is that workable?

[05:06] Erik: That seems fine. We need the benchmarking scripts so we can run them from our side too to compare.

[05:15] Liam: Absolutely. I'll prepare a Jupyter notebook and a small harness that hits the API with your prompt set and measures p50/p95/p99 and tokens. We'll also include warmup steps to populate KV cache.

[05:30] Nina: Minor transcription note — sometimes the KV cache is spoken as "K-V cash" in our docs, so just to avoid confusion.

[05:38] Liam: Ha, noted. We'll use KV cache.

[05:45] Samir: Network and VPC specifics: we are on AWS in us-west-2, peered VPCs with strict NACLs. We'll need to know if you require cross-account role or peering.

[05:57] Aisha: For Private VPC we usually do cross-account VPC peering or a transit setup. I will have our infra team outline options; Liam will include the preferred method per customer constraints.

[06:14] Olivia: On data retention — what logs or customer data is persisted? We want to ensure limited retention and the ability to disable logging for PII.

[06:25] Priya: We have configurable retention. For Private, all logs stay in customer-controlled storage if you prefer; otherwise Redwood's control plane retains minimal metadata. We'll send the retention matrix.

[06:40] Erik: Great. Who's the single point of contact on the Redwood side during the pilot?

[06:47] Priya: That'll be me for day-to-day and Liam for technical issues, Aisha for commercial/contract questions.

[06:58] [10-second pause, background keyboard sounds]

[07:10] Aisha: Let's walk through the onboarding checklist quickly. Step one: access and network - customer provides CIDR, contact for firewall, and test credentials. Step two: Redwood provisions env and shares endpoints/keys. Step three: run benchmarks and capture baselines. Step four: make adjustments, do a short run with production-like concurrency.

[07:35] Samir: For credentials, we prefer short-lived tokens. Do you have a way to rotate keys quickly for the trial?

[07:42] Liam: We support short-lived tokens and API keys rotation via the console or API. For the trial we'll issue scoped keys that you can rotate.

[07:52] Nina: On model selection — are you recommending particular model families for low-latency?

[07:58] Liam: We'll suggest a 2-3 set: a low-latency variant for realtime, a quantized mid variant for cost-sensitive throughput, and a higher-quality fallback. We'll provide performance profiles based on your token distribution.

[08:15] Olivia: Do you support function calling / structured responses? We'll need JSON output for downstream parsers.

[08:22] Liam: Yes, function/tool calling is supported. We'll include examples in the runbook.

[08:30] Erik: Any limitations on legal/compliance — like export controls or specific country requirements? We're mostly NA and EU for now, but will expand.

[08:40] Priya: For data residency we have regions in NA and EU; for Private/on-prem we can localize data. We'll capture the required compliance docs after the call.

[08:53] [small noise, someone typing]

[09:05] Aisha: Pricing during the pilot — we'll offer a usage credit and discounted dedicated rate for the committed pilot. I'll share a pricing summary. Does FoxRun have procurement timelines?

[09:18] Erik: We usually do a procurement batch at month end; we'd like to get a proposal before Aug 31, so procurement can move quickly if the pilot looks good.

[09:28] Aisha: We'll aim to get that to you by Aug 24.

[09:35] Nina: Testing considerations: warm start vs cold start — for 99th pct, do you recommend pre-warmed nodes?

[09:43] Liam: Pre-warming helps. We can do an initial warmup step in the benchmark to populate caches. For production you can configure minimum pool size.

[09:58] Samir: Observability — what traces and metrics do you expose to customers? We want per-route latency and token-level breakdowns.

[10:08] Liam: We expose token counts, per-request latency, batching size distributions, and we can hook into your tracing via OpenTelemetry. We'll provide dashboard templates for Grafana.

[10:23] Olivia: Can we get a look at the Console UI during the trial?

[10:28] Priya: Yes, we'll create staging accounts and show you the Console during the first week.

[10:35] Erik: Are there any known limitations around KV cache eviction with long-running sessions? We have sessions that keep appending context.

[10:44] Liam: The runtime manages KV cache per session; we support configured eviction and windowing policies. If you have long sessions we'll recommend periodic checkpointing or chunking. We'll include recommended settings.

[10:58] Aisha: Okay we're about a third of the way through — any blockers we should call out now?

[11:05] Samir: Network approvals may take 2 business days. Also our security team will need the SOC2 and data flow diagram.

[11:13] Priya: I'll attach the SOC2 and a data flow sketch. Erik, happy to jump into a security deep dive with your team if they'd like.

[11:22] Erik: Yes, let's do a security-focused call with our security lead after the initial materials — likely next Thursday.

[11:30] Aisha: Noted. We'll schedule a security review for 2026-08-27.

[11:38] [brief laughter]

[11:50] Liam: Quick note about fallbacks — we can configure automatic fallback to a cheaper model if latency spikes or capacity signals trigger. That keeps your app online with graceful degradation.

[12:03] Olivia: That would be useful. We'd like to test fallback behaviors in the pilot.

[12:10] Liam: We'll include failure-mode tests in the benchmark plan.

[12:20] Nina: Regarding data sampling for the pilot, we'll sanitize and provide a set of ~500 representative prompts and a few larger batches. Is that enough?

[12:30] Liam: That's perfect — send them in a CSV or JSONL and we'll wire them into the harness.

[12:38] [20-second pause, typing noises]

[12:58] Aisha: Let's do a short recap and the explicit next steps. Priya, can you read back?

[13:06] Priya: Sure. Action items: Liam to send the benchmark harness and runbook by 2026-08-25; Aisha to send pricing summary and trial details by 2026-08-24; Erik to share network diagram and CIDR by 2026-08-26; Samir to arrange VPC access; Olivia to confirm success metrics and sample data by 2026-08-27. We'll schedule a security deep dive for 2026-08-27 and benchmarking week for 2026-08-31.

[13:38] Erik: That's accurate. One more ask — can you include a simple rollback plan if we see regressions during rollout?

[13:47] Liam: Yes. We'll document rollback steps and an automatic fallback policy that can be toggled.

[13:55] Aisha: Anything else from the customer side?

[14:00] Nina: Nothing else from me. Excited to get started.

[14:04] Samir: Same. We'll prioritize network access so we can hit the timeline.

[14:08] Aisha: Great — thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the materials. Meeting adjourned.

[14:15] [meeting ends]

Notes about transcript: occasional mis-transcribes present, speaker labels inferred from calendar; timestamps approximate to aid navigation.
notes: Customer is leaning toward Private VPC with dedicated trial. Priority metrics: p99 latency <350ms for short prompts and cost under threshold. Procurement deadline: Aug 31. Security deep-dive requested.
